_meta.design: Wave 4 — the horizon made machine-visible. Wave 3 shipped the doctrine (plan only to the knowledge horizon; end with an explicit replan point) as WORDS: the how-to's replan point is a convention ('a final task whose gate verifies the learning is recorded') and its audit teeth are an aspiration ('the plan refuter should flag it the way hb-audit flags test -f'). No machine part knows what a horizon is — 'horizon' appears zero times in either runtime — so finishing a deliberately-short plan is indistinguishable from finishing a complete project: the resolver returns all_done, the tick congratulates, the exec driver prints DONE. This wave gives the doctrine its mechanism: (1) a first-class marker — "horizon": true on the final planned phase (type-checked by both lints; position never linted — an inert historical flag after an append is sanctioned); (2) the reached horizon is distinguished from the done project — the resolver returns a NEW type replan_pending when every live phase is complete and the last live phase is flagged and unclosed, the tick wakes it ONCE (the all-done-alerted precedent, never a busy-loop) as a human-needed reason with exactly TWO sanctioned moves: replan by append-continuation (T184's proven surface) or END the project through a recorded decision — hb horizon close --reason <why>, fail-closed (reached + flagged + unclosed + reasoned + the live list non-empty + NO open regate cycle in any state on a live gate, else nonzero exit and NO event), appending a phase-scoped horizon_closed event that survives rebuild and projects SPARSELY (existing projections stay byte-identical); (3) the aspiration made real — hb-audit's speculative_tail names the fabricated-far-phases shape (a gated head, then >= 2 trailing unverified live phases) and the exact cut point. Honest limits pinned, not hidden: the marker is PLAN surface — desc-class, unpinned by the drift tripwire — so deleting the flag from the completed phase, or parking it, silences the wake; the proof pins that silence as behavior and parity-notes + the how-to record it; the recorded path is the close verb. Pre-checked: 'horizon' absent from both runtimes; T185 unused; the 9 docs h2w pins are prose-clean today (ALL-PROSE-OK verified); heartbeat.md has no exposure (untouched); both exec drivers already fail closed on unknown reasons (the named case adds honesty, not new safety); the SKILL reason-table row and the hook stop-list edits land in H1 and GATE_H1 runs their checkers DIRECTLY (h1s: single-source.sh + hook-drives-loop.sh — T138.1/T143 would otherwise bind first at h2y's full suite, a whole-phase red window); dev-plugin.md ll.100/156/160/201 enumerate the resolver types and protocol reasons this wave extends and are falsified rows to RE-SPECIFY (dev-python's twins located at fold time); a speculative_tail probe over all 63 planning dags, the seeded template and the test fixtures fires on NONE (no suite reddens); PROTOCOL.md is bootstrap-generated from the hb.js map (no second template surface). The H2 marker is the plan practicing its own doctrine — wave 5 is genuinely unplanned — but the live .hb runs bootstrap-time COPIES of the tools, so the wake itself is proven in fixtures; the repo's own plan sees it only after a sanctioned tool refresh (a release-time chore, outside gate scope).

tasks.description: Write tests/horizon.sh with the env-hygiene header VERBATIM (unset HB_DIR PROJECT_DIR GATE G DAG_FILE EVENTS_FILE 2>/dev/null || true). Fixtures are built in mktemp from the repo's templates (the tests/replan.sh pattern); never against the repo's own .hb. Cases: (marker) a project whose last phase carries "horizon": true, completed through the CLI with criteria-pinned passes — both resolvers return {"type":"replan_pending","phase":<id>} with identical keys (m1); both ticks wake replan_pending ONCE with a data.action that NAMES both sanctioned moves (grep the append path and the close verb in the action text, not mere non-emptiness) and the SECOND tick sleeps replan_waiting (m2); the same fixture without the marker verdicts all_done on both (m3 — the regression pin); both exec drivers print 'HB-EXEC STOP: replan_pending' and exit nonzero (HB_EXEC_BACKEND=script HB_EXEC_CMD='cat >/dev/null') (m4). (close) hb horizon close is fail-closed on BOTH runtimes: refused with a nonzero exit and NO appended event when the horizon is not reached (c1), when --reason is missing/empty (c2), when already closed per the PROJECTED state.horizon_closed — the resolver's own source, and the c5 probe pins ONE source: close, append an 'initialized' event, REPLAY the completion history after the reset (re-append the task_done/gate_passed events — the proj_compare 'mid' precedent; bare replayed passes never pin, so the replay is drift-safe), then both runtimes must re-verdict replan_pending AND re-accept a close (a projection read sees the reset; a log scan still sees the old event and wedges) (c5), and when any live gate's regate cycle is open in ANY state — pending (declared), unanswered in the log, or REARMED WITHOUT A FRESH PASS (the stale-rearm window every verdict-class sibling refuses) (c6 — probe all FOUR shapes on both runtimes: declare → refused; declare then HAND-CLEAR the marker in the mktemp dag → STILL refused, the log is truth (the unanswered-regate clause isolated); rearm alone → STILL refused; fresh criteria-pinned pass → the close reopens); the close on an ALL-PARKED plan takes the not-reached refusal, never a throw (c7); a valid close appends horizon_closed carrying phase, reason and the recording HB_ACTOR, reprojects state.json (horizon_closed: [<phase>] present; ABSENT on every fixture with no close event — the sparse-projection pin), and the next tick verdicts all_done (c3); hb rebuild preserves the verdict (c4). (append) at a reached horizon, appending fresh phases (first new gate_entry = the completed horizon phase's gate_exit) makes both ticks hand out the appended tasks (a1); the old flag is inert mid-plan — no replan wake while appended work remains (a2); completing an appended plan whose own last phase is flagged wakes replan_pending for the NEW phase even though the OLD phase has a recorded close (a3 — the close is phase-scoped); a STALE once-flag never silences a newer horizon — after the first wake (flag set), append and complete the new phases entirely through the CLI with NO intermediate tick, and the next tick must still wake replan_pending for the NEW phase (the flag stores the phase id) (a4). (limits) deleting the flag from the completed phase (l1) or parking the flagged phase (l2) verdicts all_done with doctor QUIET on both runtimes — the honest limit pinned as behavior. (parked-out) an ALL-PARKED plan verdicts all_done on both runtimes — no crash, no eternal no_pending_tasks sleep — including when the flag sits on a parked phase (p1). (lint) a non-boolean horizon is a lint ERROR with byte-identical messages (n1); "horizon": true and false lint at 0 errors, including true on a NON-final phase (inert — n2). tasks.title: implement the mechanism (resolver, projection, ticks, close verb, protocol, exec, report)
tasks.description: Implement the mechanism on both runtimes, logic mirrored exactly, every guard marker (horizon-guard: resolver / tick / close) on a strip-clean SINGLE line that is a complete statement (python lines never a block header — the IndentationError class). RESOLVER (hb-next-task.js resolve + resolver.py resolve): in the all-live-phases-complete branch, when the LAST live phase carries horizon === true and its id is not in state.horizon_closed, return {"type":"replan_pending","phase":<id>} — identical keys; every other shape keeps returning all_done, EXPLICITLY including the empty live list (an all-parked plan has no last live phase — today's all_done behavior, never a throw that tick.sh would swallow into a no_pending_tasks sleep). PROJECTION (hb.js project + state.py project): a horizon_closed event adds its phase to a set ('initialized' resets it, the existing precedent); project it SPARSELY — s.horizon_closed only when non-empty, insertion-ordered — so every existing projection stays byte-identical. TICK (tick.sh + tick.py): a replan_pending resolution wakes ONCE (flag file .replan-alerted, the .all-done-alerted precedent; tick.sh also notifies 'replan_pending' and updates the header's notify-reason comment, folding the comment's missing criteria_drift in the same edit — the F5 currency-debt class), then sleeps {"reason":"replan_waiting"}; the flag STORES THE HORIZON PHASE ID — a wake for a DIFFERENT phase ignores a stale flag and rewrites it (so an append completed entirely through the CLI with no intermediate tick can never be permanently silenced) — and is cleared on the task and all_done branches; no event is appended on the wake (the log records decisions, not notifications). CLOSE VERB (hb.js case 'horizon' + a cli.py 'horizon' parser): hb horizon close --reason <why> under the write lock — the close is an ACCEPTANCE verb and sits inside the regate fail-closed perimeter like its siblings (anchor, review, constraints --record): refused (nonzero exit, NO event appended) when the subaction is not 'close', when --reason is missing/empty, when the last live phase is not flagged, when any live phase is incomplete, when the live list is EMPTY (the not-reached refusal — never a throw on an all-parked plan), when that phase is already in the PROJECTED state.horizon_closed (one source — the resolver's), or when any live gate's regate cycle is open in any state — pending (regateBlocks), unanswered in the log, or rearmed WITHOUT a fresh criteria-pinned pass (staleRearm — the verdict-class perimeter: hb review and both executors refuse this exact window; the close is a verdict, not a record); on success append {"event":"horizon_closed","phase":...,"reason":...} (actor via the existing appendEvent attribution), reproject, print the confirmation; both usage strings gain the verb. PROTOCOL (every wave-3 surface): a replan_pending row in hb.js PROTOCOL and protocol.py with identical KEYS and runtime-flavored action text naming BOTH sanctioned moves (replan by append-continuation — plan only the NEXT horizon — or hb horizon close --reason <why> as the recorded end-of-project decision) and never a third path — and never a quoted key-colon substring like a literal '"horizon":' in the action or SKILL-row text (single-source.sh extracts protocol keys with a key-colon grep); .hb/PROTOCOL.md regenerates from the table; SKILL.md's reason table gains the row (T138.1 forces it; the surrounding prose is H2's); hb-exec.js and executor.py gain a NAMED replan_pending case (escalate / 'HB-EXEC STOP: replan_pending', exit nonzero — both drivers already fail closed on unknown reasons, the named case is honesty); heartbeat-detect.sh's two stop lists gain replan_pending keeping docs/howto/gate-examples/hook-drives-loop.sh green (T143's checker, which h1s runs at the gate); mcp_server.py's tick-tool description likewise. REPORT (hb-report.js + report.py): one horizon line when the last live phase is flagged — planned / REACHED (naming both sanctioned moves) / closed by <actor>: <reason> — and no line otherwise.

tasks.title: implement the teeth (lint marker type rule, audit speculative_tail)
tasks.description: Implement the static teeth, rulesets mirrored byte-exact. LINT (hb-lint.js + lint.py): a phase carrying a non-boolean horizon is an ERROR — '[<pid>] horizon must be true or false (the knowledge-horizon marker)' (the regate.pending precedent, degenerate phase ids rendered '?' at the existing sites); true/false pass, and position is NOT linted (an inert historical flag after an append is sanctioned — the how-to documents inertness). AUDIT (hb-audit.js + audit.py): the speculative_tail rule — over LIVE phases in plan order, a phase is 'unverified' when it has tasks but no gate_exit, when it has NO tasks and no gate_exit (a placeholder is the purest speculative shape), when its gate has no criteria, or when its gate has zero behavioral criteria (reusing classify; hostile shapes ride the existing not-behavioral normalization, never a crash); when the maximal TRAILING run of unverified phases has length >= 2 AND at least one earlier live phase is verified, emit ONE warn finding (rule 'speculative_tail', anchored on the first tail phase) naming the tail ids, the cut phase (the last verified phase) and the cure — end the plan there with "horizon": true and plan the tail when its spec is known — citing docs/howto/plan-to-the-horizon.md; quiet on the t2–t5 shapes. Severity stays warn: the hollow members already carry their own per-phase errors, and this rule's job is the DIAGNOSIS (the cut point), not a second sentence. The seeded template dag and every fixture dag the suites audit must stay speculative_tail-quiet (check, don't assume), with the one marker line this wave adds to its own plan file linting clean.

constraints.claim: The reached horizon is distinguished from the done project, exactly: on both runtimes, when every live phase is complete and the LAST live phase carries horizon === true with its id not in the projected state.horizon_closed, resolve returns {type:'replan_pending', phase} with identical keys and the tick wakes replan_pending ONCE (a second un-cured tick sleeps replan_waiting; data.action injected from the protocol names both sanctioned moves); with no marker, a deleted flag, a parked horizon phase, a recorded close, or an EMPTY live list (an all-parked plan — never a throw), the verdict is all_done; after an append the resolver hands out the new phases (the old flag inert) and a newly reached appended horizon wakes again — a stale once-flag from an earlier horizon never silences it (the flag stores the phase id); the horizon_closed projection is SPARSE — a log with no horizon_closed event projects a state.json without the key, byte-identical to today's projection.
constraints.violation: Any listed shape returns the wrong verdict on either runtime or the runtimes diverge on keys; an all-parked plan crashes a resolver (or sleeps no_pending_tasks forever); the wake repeats without a cure, never fires for a reached horizon, or stays silenced by a stale flag after an untick'd append; a horizon-less project's state.json gains a key or changes a byte (beyond last_updated).

constraints.claim: The close is a recorded, fail-closed, phase-scoped VERDICT on both runtimes, inside the full regate perimeter like its verdict-class siblings (hb review, both executors): hb horizon close requires a non-empty --reason, a reached horizon (all live phases complete, the live list non-empty — an all-parked plan takes the not-reached refusal, never a throw — and the last live phase flagged), no prior close for that phase in the PROJECTED state.horizon_closed (the resolver's own source — never a second, log-scan reading; c5's initialized-reset-then-replay probe distinguishes the implementations), and NO open regate cycle in any state on any live gate — pending, unanswered in the log, or rearmed without a fresh criteria-pinned pass (the stale-rearm window) — each refusal exits nonzero and appends NO event; a valid close appends horizon_closed {phase, reason} under the existing actor attribution, reprojects, and the verdict survives hb rebuild; a close recorded for an earlier horizon phase never quiets a later appended one.
constraints.violation: A refused close appends an event or exits 0; an early, reason-less, unflagged or double close is accepted on either runtime; a close is accepted while a live gate's regate cycle is open — pending, unanswered, OR rearmed without a fresh pass (the revision retired behind a 'finished' project); the close throws on an all-parked plan; the refusal and the resolver read different sources (the initialized-reset wedge — c5's probe sequence fails); the close is lost on rebuild; an old close silences a new horizon.

constraints.claim: The loudness reaches every surface and the limits are stated where they bind: both exec drivers STOP on replan_pending with a NAMED escalation (HB-EXEC STOP: replan_pending, nonzero exit, never a busy-loop); the reason lives with identical keys on every protocol surface — hb.js PROTOCOL, protocol.py, the regenerated PROTOCOL.md, SKILL.md's reason table (T138.1 green), both exec case tables, heartbeat-detect.sh's stop lists (T143 green), mcp_server.py's tick description; both reports print the horizon line (planned / REACHED naming both sanctioned moves / closed by actor: reason) and nothing on an unmarked project; and the honest limits (flag deletion and parking silence the wake — plan surface, unpinned by the drift tripwire; the recorded path is the close verb) are pinned by the proof and recorded in parity-notes.
constraints.violation: A driver proceeds or busy-loops past a reached horizon; any protocol surface omits replan_pending or its action text invents a third path (or permits closing as an escape from an unreached horizon); the reports stay silent on a reached horizon or invent lines on unmarked projects; a stop-list edit reddens T143 or the SKILL row reddens T138.1; the limits go unrecorded.

constraints.claim: The teeth and the proof's hygiene are exact: both lints error byte-identically on a non-boolean horizon and stay at 0 errors on true/false and on an inert non-final flag; both audits emit speculative_tail exactly once (warn) iff >= 2 trailing live phases are unverified (unguarded / ungated / zero-behavioral / the zero-task zero-gate placeholder) AND at least one earlier live phase is verified — naming the tail ids, the cut phase and the horizon cure — and stay quiet on a fully-gated plan, a single unverified final phase, an all-unverified plan, and a parked tail, without crashing on hostile criteria shapes and without firing on any existing planning dag, the seeded template, or a suite fixture; the selftest sabotages redden the NAMED checks (markers strip-clean, python markers complete statements); T185's suite checks key on HORIZON-OK / HORIZON-SELFTEST-OK; the four parity cases (resolve, project, lint, audit) are non-vacuous, implemented inline, and leave the audit fixture loop's count (T137's pin) untouched.
constraints.violation: A rule misfires or stays silent on a listed shape, crashes, or its message bytes differ between runtimes; a sabotage passes or reddens the wrong check (or for a parse error instead of the named reason); a T185 check would pass on a red run; a parity case passes on two empty or identical-error outputs.
